To detect Cu²⁺, we can add ammonia (NH₃ 1 M) to a fresh aliquot of the original sample; Cu²⁺ forms a deep‑blue tetraamminecopper(II) complex, giving a characteristic blue solution. If no blue color appears, Cu²⁺ is absent and the remaining cation is likely a metal that forms a white hydroxide (e.g., Zn²⁺ or Mg²⁺) which would have been masked in the earlier KOH test. Therefore, I will add NH₃ to a fresh portion of the sample and observe.</thought>

    "sol2_label": "NH3(1M)",
    "sol2_vol": 1
